lines.english: "Hey～ can someone get that real quick?"
"Ah, no, that won't do. Hang on for a second! This part's sliding off!"
"The bento boxes have arrived～ Whoever's free should eat up as soon as they can."
"So it's finally time."
"After three years of planning, three months of scriptwriting, and one month of production… Senouchi Akira's life work is finally complete."
"…I suppose this is where I die, then."
"Well, all jokes aside, you did work so hard that it wouldn't be surprising if you collapsed at any moment now."
"Not really, it's just the usual."
"This particular performance is special. Not a single person who supported you quit. Usually, at least five people would quit after each public performance."
"I was being more selfish than I usually was, though."
"Yeah… you went even more overboard than usual as well. You pushed yourself right to the edge of collapsing, but that attitude of yours must have made an impression on the others as well."
"Not really. Not a single thing I did was for you or any of the other members, President."
"It doesn't matter what exactly you pushed yourself so far for. Even when you're struggling, you still desperately try your best to move forward, and that's what moved everyone, Princess."
"…What do you mean?"
"I didn't notice this right before rehearsal since everything seemed normal, but I was quite surprised when I walked into the clubroom just a moment ago…"
"Aaah～"
"Well, I've forbidden anyone from entering for the time being. It'll probably take a whole day to clean up that mess."
"I've sent the laptop for repairs. …But from the looks of things, I imagine we'll need to buy a new one."
"I'll compensate for it, okay? …So don't tell me to change how I'm acting. …Don't even try to correct me, either."
"We're about to present the real performance. Things like this happen. I'm not mad about this or anything."
"Alright, then."
"So you didn't make up with your boyfriend in the end, huh? You skipped practice the whole day yesterday just so you could meet him, right?"
"…I don't know what you're talking about."
"So that trump card of yours didn't end up working, did it? I bet he couldn't bring himself to trust you because you just acted the way you usually do, right?"
"…President."
"Wait, no, I was just trying to lighten the mood before the show with some banter! It was all just a joke, I wasn't serious about any of that!"
"There's no need for you to worry about me. My personal life won't hinder my performance on stage at all."
"Well, based on what you've accomplished up until now, I can believe that."
"As you wish, President, I'll show you my best performance today…"
"And this has nothing to do with your personal life, I take it."
"There's only four hours left until the live performance. It's about time we finished setting everything up～"
"Well, I plan on going back to the waiting room… What are you going to do, Princess?"
"I'll stay here a little longer for now."
"Isn't it cold here? Will you be alright?"
"I'm fine."
"Even if you say you're alright, Princess, the one in your belly…"
"Uh, well, see you at rehearsal, then."
"The whole reason why it's called a trump card is because you're supposed to save it until the very end…"
Although it's going to be March by tomorrow, the way the wind pierces my skin suggests that there's still quite a long time before the first day of spring will arrive.
Keeping true to the weather forecast, the sky is shrouded by gloomy, ashen clouds, such that my sense of time feels distorted.
…It's hard to believe it's only 1 PM right now.
But the weather isn't the only reason why my sense of time feels distorted.

It's the last day of February, and university students have entered their spring break, while high school students are transitioning to self-studying, given that the entrance exam period has passed and their results have been released.

This station is the second nearest to my university, and it was never really a prosperous area to begin with. It feels as if there's more than a small trickle of people coming and going no matter the time.
A florist single-mindedly tends to her flowers illuminated by the dim lighting of her store, seemingly unconcerned about the prospect of any customers visiting.
A part-timer middle-aged lady diligently stocks the shelves of a supermarket's storefront.
An elderly person leisurely strolls by the shopping district without a destination in mind, accompanied by a girl who seems to be their granddaughter pushing their wheelchair.
Nothing has changed since I enrolled in high school. I'm witnessing the same scenery as if time never passed here in this station that's only fifteen minutes away from the school grounds by foot.
I've noticed that the florist has more gray hairs on her head, though. And I've noticed that the number of stores that are still operating within this district has reduced by about three.
And the braided girl who worked part-time in the supermarket…
"I'm sorry for being late."
"Well, I just ended up coming early, that's all. …You're right on time."
"I knew you would arrive 30 minutes in advance, Haruki-kun, yet I couldn't make it in time. I'm sorry."
"…Haha."
She quit her job three years ago to become the singer of a certain band for a school festival…
"Audio is a-okay!"
"Alright, stop the music! Let's set things up for Act One～"
"The stage setting doesn't seem to have any problems. Everything is going according to plan so far."
"This is a miracle."
"This is the first time something like this has happened in the two years since I've joined this troupe."
"It's actually concerning that things are going so smoothly. I hope nothing horrible happens during the actual performance, of course…"
"We're just getting more and more experienced!"
"Well, I think so too. Things were quite difficult for us back when we were still amateurs. Didn't we only have like five people during our first public performance?"
"We even asked people from other clubs to help us out. …We didn't just need folks to help out backstage, but we also needed a candidate for our male lead."
"But we got into a big pickle again even after that performance, given that two people ended up quitting, and we took flak from other clubs…"
"Ah, but I was really moved by that first public performance! I immediately decided to join after witnessing it."
"…Well, it's the same for me."
"The fact that you two joined the troupe really helped us out. There's no doubt that we would've just disbanded otherwise."
"That's because Senouchi-san was really amazing back then. I wanted to perform with her no matter what…"
"…You can say that again."
"We have to keep working hard… We've already come this far, after all."
"That's right. No matter what happens, and regardless of who we'll be missing…"
"…By the way, President, how are things with you and university? Are you graduating? Or are you getting expelled?"
"Ah, now that you mention it, isn't the graduation ceremony tomorrow? Even so…"
"It seems you won't be able to graduate. In other words, you won't be able to assume the role of someone who manages a club within Houjou University…"
"W-What are you saying!? I have no intention of letting this Watos Troupe end as just some university drama club, you know?"
"No, that's not the problem here. I was just wondering if you had to deal with stuff like negotiations and procedures concerning the university…"
"For instance, will you be able to rent this north hall despite not being considered a registered student?"
"And you guys were going on saying that you'll all continue to work hard just a moment ago!"
"No, President… these are completely separate matters…"
"Uh… it's about time to start rehearsal, you know? There's less than two hours until our public performance."
"Ah～ sorry, sorry. Alright～ let's get our final rehearsal started～! Lower the curtains～!"
"Are you ready, Princess…?"
"…Absolutely."
"…Why are you looking so pale? You're sweating quite a bit as well."
"I wonder if I'm getting too engrossed… and it's supposed to be just rehearsal."
"…You're giving me that explanation?"
"Hey, could we have a look over here this time?"
"H-Here?"
"Ah… I suppose you might feel a little uncomfortable about entering a shop like this, Haruki-kun? It does look like a shop that caters only to girls."
"N-No, that's not the issue here…"
"What is it? You're sweating all of a sudden."
"…I-It's nothing. Alright, let's go in."
"Ah, you don't have to force yourself. It's not like there's something I specifically want to buy in here."
"No, I'm not forcing myself. Really, I, well… let's go."
"Ah, h-hang on, Haruki-ku…"
"Welcome… ah, it's nice to see you again!"
"Eh?"
"Hello, it's been a while… I see you actually remember me."
"Eh? Eh?"
"Of course. I'd never forget the face of a customer who's made a purchase here."
That can't be true, strictly speaking. Though to be fair, it'd be quite ridiculous of me to expect her to remember me after more than three years.
"Haruki-kun, this is…"
"Umm… look over there."
As Setsuna felt puzzled about the situation, I pointed at the corner of one of the display cases.
"Eh… ahh!"
And Setsuna's reaction is exactly how I imagined it to be.
She's now constantly looking at her left wrist and comparing what she's wearing on it with the item inside the display case.
"Are you looking for a present today as well?"
"Ah, not really…"
"But today, it seems you don't have to fuss over what to do for more than two hours like last time, right?"
"Hold on!"
"Fu, fufu…"
"I-I'm sorry, Haruki-kun. I couldn't read the mood there… umm…"
"No, I'd be more surprised if you did manage to read it."
Everything's been completely exposed.
The price of the gift I gave her and the store I bought it from, as well as how long I ended up fussing over whether or not to buy it.
"H-Hey, I really don't mind this at all, you know? Rather, I'm actually quite happy to learn about this."
"I-Is that so…"
I'm sure she's not lying.
After all, Setsuna's been fondly stroking the bracelet on her left wrist ever since she walked out of the shop.
She never stopped even after she discovered that it was nothing more than a cheap product.
"That salesperson is an interesting person, isn't she? Normally, they wouldn't spend over two hours with the same customer, you know?"
"I was the only male customer in the shop back then, so I wonder if she thought about teasing me a little…"
The time gradually flew by as I found myself mesmerized by Setsuna's smile and cheerful tone.
After meeting up at Suetsugu-chou Station, we took the train to the city and shared a meal together.
We remained in the restaurant until lunchtime ended, and then we went window shopping at the station building.
We talked, laughed and walked side by side without reservation, as if we had returned to how things were between us three years ago.
No matter how I look at it… we've been on a date that's meant for us to make up with one another.
"Are you cold?"
"Just a little."
"I… see."
We'd been maintaining a complicated distance between one another throughout the past three years.
That is, until three months ago, when our relationship finally broke down.
And on the exact same day we collapsed, I committed the unthinkable by seeking the comfort of another woman.
However, in only a month, I ended up being betrayed by that woman.
The very same woman who slathered me all over with honeyed lies and tempted me to fall into the depths of hell…
But in the end, the one who picked me back up and saved me without a word after I've fallen so deep was Setsuna, who's right in front of me right now.
She's the one who helped me recover physically when I was crippled by a fever, and she's the one who gave me the willpower to overcome the emotional scars that resurfaced due to that same illness.
"Hey, Setsuna…"
"Hm?"
"Are you getting tired? What do you say to getting some tea?"
"Yeah… if that's fine with you, Haruki-kun."
That's why our date meant for us to make up is still continuing.
And it will keep going on for as long as Setsuna and I want it to.
That's why… if we keep this up until spring arrives, and then summer, and then autumn…
And if we promised now that we would share in the joy of finding our respective jobs, talking about the future, and celebrating our graduation together…
Perhaps in a year from now, we'd even be able to welcome a bright future together.
The three years we've spent up until now would be nothing more than a bad dream to us.
"The crowd sure is pouring in. We made the right choice by taking the chairs out."
"It was clear from the number of people in line before opening that there would have to be standing spectators as well. I wonder if we'll set another viewership record again?"
"I'm not the leader of this troupe, but I'd say it'd be a waste for it to end as some university club."
"So long as we have Senouchi Akira… we could probably make a living off this even in other public theaters."
"That'd be quite the sight to see. Sure, it'd probably be hard at first since we'd be starting out in the red, but if we work hard and maintain the pace we have now, the fans will recognize it…"
"Still, she's quite fickle, so she could suddenly decide to participate in some film and we'd break up on the spot."
"That sounds like something that could really happen…"
"…Tanaka."
"Um, please consider letting me join."
"It's not about that, it's about today's show. Be prepared to get on stage at a moment's notice."
"…This is only the first day, you know?"
"There's… something wrong with the princess."
"…Are you okay?"
"…What do you mean?"
"Nothing, you just look a little giddy."
"Well, that's just how you're looking at the situation. You're so nervous that you can't even stand straight right now, can you?"
"Please don't joke around like that. I know I'm not fully prepared, but I'm not as nervous as you think I am, either."
"Is that so…"
"I have absolutely no intention of dragging you down whatsoever. You can put your faith in me."
"…Yoshida."
"Please don't mock me with that smile of yours. It'll really affect my motivation."
"I had no intention of mocking you. …I just want to tell you something in advance."
"You want to… tell me something?"
"You know, Yoshida…"
"Y-Yeah…"
"From this point on, I'll love you and adore you so much that I'll be consumed by it."
"I'll stop at nothing and struggle with all my might just so I can have you. And I'll become so obsessed with you my efforts will end up biting me in the back."
"Ah…"
"That's the sort of foolish woman I'll become… So please, just for these few hours, please love me with all you got…"
"And then, I want you to be wounded to the core of your heart by the conclusion that this foolish woman has chosen… You can do that for me, can't you?"
"A-Alright!"
"You're not supposed to say 'alright,' but 'yeah'… Kazuki-kun."
"…Yeah, I understand."
"Mhm…"
"Thank you for your patience. Watos Troupe's spring performance, Todokanai Koi, is about to begin."
"…Do your best, Yukine. Let's enjoy our stage… to its fullest."
"Thank you… Kazuki-kun."
"Who's the foolish woman here?"
"Ogiso Setsuna? Touma Kazusa?"
"Or is it…"
Act One, Scene One.
Nishimura Kazuki found himself troubled because a band competition sponsored by a certain musical instrument manufacturer was coming up next month.
He had once vowed that he would make a debut with a major label company, but the band he had enlisted for the competition broke up due to a petty conflict caused by a female member of the group.
Thus, Kazuki was left with nothing to do but practice with his guitar in an empty classroom at sunset.
And all that accompanied him was the melody of a piano performed by an unknown pianist from the classroom next to the one he was in.
But on that day…
While enjoying his customary, carefree jam session with the neighboring pianist, Kazuki noticed yet another, unfamiliar sound joining in together with them.
It was not the sound of a musical instrument, but the vibrant, clear singing voice of a girlーone that would perfectly fit the role that he desperately needed to have filled at the moment.
"You are…"
"Eh? Ah, me? Um…"
"Could you be… the guitarist?"
"Uh, mhm, um… Class 3-E, Nishimura Kazuki."
"I see. So you two were the ones playing White Album."
"Well, yeah. It was me and… someone else I'm not familiar with."
"It's an old song… but I really like it. …Don't you feel the same way?"
"This is the first song I learned how to play… My friends always teased me about how I was a bandwagoning poser, though."
"Ah… Me too! It was the first song I ever sang when I went to karaoke for the first time! …I think both the boys and girls really liked it, though."
"…Ah, I see."
"Ah, I'm sorry. I haven't told you my name yet. Nice to meet you, Guitar-san. I'm…"
"I told you, I'm Nishimura."
Act One, Scene Two.
Her name is Hatsushiba Yukine.
Blessed with popularity and good looks, she's easily recognized by anyone as the school's number one beauty.
She's also considered a mysterious student within her grade, given her contradictory personality of having a bright demeanor while also being rather distant in her relationships at the same time.
But as for her true self…

She's actually an amiable and family-oriented girl, and she can't bring herself to fully relinquish the label of being the school beauty that's been forced upon her, for she was just a little vain at heart.
She also has a perfectly common hobby: karaoke.
Nevertheless, she spends her days in discontent. Placed on such a high pedestal in school, she's had to change her pastimes and personality so as to not reveal her hobby to anyone.
And thus, her hobby became karaokeーrather, her hobby became "enjoying karaoke by herself."
"Um, the starting chord for this song is…"
"Ah, I know that one!"
"Huh, you know about it even though you never played it before?"
"Yeah, it's 2428-02, isn't it?"
"…Huh?"
"Ah, that's at my regular spot, Hyper Jam… Kazuki-kun, do you go to X3600? Or P-Kara?"
"What kind of code was that!?"
There were minor adjustments to the story's setting, but the opening act unfolded in a way that was almost identical to its original counterpart.
However, the script's tone is also a lot more comedic in comparison, and the heroine was portrayed as being rather silly.

The amateur singer who's good at singing but only has her cuteness going for her, and the stubborn guitarist who's knowledgeable but very mediocre. They didn't seem to be on the same wavelength during practice.
As she continues to spend more and more time with Kazuki, Yukine's facade of a beauty placed on a high pedestal also gradually peels away.
But at some point, she also comes to enjoy the fact that Kazuki can see through it and appreciate her true self.
"Goodness me… I'm not that scatter-brained…"
Act One, Scene Three.
The group has now assembled a guitarist and a singer. Even so, they don't think that they have enough members yet.
If they want to participate in the competition, they still require a bassist and a drummer, at the very least.
There's only three weeks left until the competition… That's why Kazuki is desperate for experienced candidates to fill the role of bassist and drummer.
…At least, that's how things should've gone.
"…So, what business do you have coming all the way here, Nishimura?"
"Well, you're good with the piano, right…"
"That doesn't answer my question."
"If you're this good, then you can definitely make it within three weeks. Yes! I found our keyboardist!"
"Weren't you looking for a bassist and a drummer?"
"Fuyuki, I'm begging you! Please join our band!"
"Are you even listening to me?"
"It doesn't matter what instrument you'll be playing! What really matters in a band is that all its members work well together, right?"
"…And what makes you think we work well together?"
"Because you're the only one who can go along with my guitar playing!"
"Then answer my question."
"Only someone as skilled as you can cover for my lousy performance on the guitar!"
"…I suppose I should commend you for the fact that you're able to rationally gauge your own ability, but that's all the more reason for you to consider the position you're in right now."
"Even so, I still want you to join, Fuyuki. In fact, I won't accept anyone other than you!"
"Knock it off with the boorish flattery. You're actually giving me chills."
"But it was you, wasn't it? You're the one who's been accompanying me with your piano all this time whenever I was feeling down."
"…I don't know what you're talking about."
Act One, Scene Four.
Her name is Fuyuki Haruna.
With an infamous streak that's a stark contrast to Yukine's popularity despite their rivaling looks, she boasts a dominant presence in the school. Though an unsettling one, at that.
She's an untouchable, a piano prodigy immune to any interference from the teachers due to her mother's influence as a famous pianist.
But as for her true self…
She's the mysterious pianist who always accompanies the protagonist's terrible guitar playing from the neighboring classroom.
She's the one who sits right next to the protagonist in class, and she's actually quite compassionate despite her unapproachable exterior.
Though her compassion only ever seems to be for Kazuki alone.
"Ouch!?"
"Start over, from the top."
"F-Fine…"
"You know, if you can't even play this part without any mistakes, your demo tape will probably get a fail on the preliminary round."
"Ah, well, we already passed that, so that won't be an issue… It's just that I wasn't the guitarist at the time."

"…Why did I of all people get involved with you, anyway? It's pretty obvious that this band is going to be nothing more than the laughingstock of the contest. And to think I've never finished below second place in any of my own competitions."
"You really are amazing, Fuyuki."
"…Well, that's all in the past. Come on, keep playing."
"Yeah…"
"Hey, Nishimura."
"Why are you so hell-bent on signing on with a major record label or whatever? For all the effort you're putting in, you're barely improving at all."
"…Was that a question, or did you just mock me?"
"Well, take it as a question."
"I guess… Maybe I just want to leave my mark on the world?
…Ouch!?"
"W-Wait a second! Why did you hit me when I gave you a serious answer!?"
"What sort of far-fetched nonsense are you saying with such a serious look on your face!? Sheesh, I got goosebumps! That was disgusting!"
"I-Is it really all that weird? I mean, every man should set a goal like that for himself at least once in his life, don't you think?"
"I think you'd be better off saying you just want to be popular with the girls, don't you think?"
"All of my old friends said the same thing… My goal had them rolling on the floor laughing. I was the worst at playing out of all of us, after all."
"Why would you want to leave a mark in the first place? …Are you really that happy to be alive right now?"
"…Scratch that. Never mind. Just forget it."
"Uh, huh…?"
"Anyway, well, that's an admirable goal you've got. Go for it. It's just too dazzling of a goal for me to ever understand, though."
"I see, you don't get it, huh… Yukine seemed to understand it, though."
"…Yukine?"
"She even said that she'd support me forever. She even said that she'd be my number one fan."
"You're quite the realist, then. But it's such a waste of your talent. If you would just dare to dream a little bigger…
Whoa!?"
"W-Wait… Hey!"
"Why? Tell me why!"
Fans of this theater troupe probably already know about what's going on. And they're enjoying themselves despite being fully aware of that fact.
They knew that all of the main heroines in the play are portrayed by Senouchi Akira.

The fact that the story's set up in a way that neither of the heroines have any interaction with one anotherーand the fact that she's acting out both of their roles by herselfーfully demonstrates her peerless skill as an actress.

Up until a while ago, the famous actress was playing the first heroine who was bright and charming in character, but now she's portraying the second heroine who's gloomy and hostile, and she's really making the two roles feel distinct.

I'd note, however, that she's also planned for this second character to behave just a little more violently than her real counterpart, just so her emotions are easier to understand in a stage setting…
"Kazusa wasn't that unreasonable of a girl, was she?"
"You think so? That's pretty much how she always acted, though. And she was pretty scary at that."
"Jeez…"
Twisted as she was, the genius pianist possessed skill and knowledge that far surpassed that of the mediocre guitarist, and she continued to bully the latter under the pretense of special training.
And yet he desperately clung to said special training, as if he'd been waiting for those very days to come, and worked on improving his skills.
With the two spending more and more time alone together, their hearts grew ever closer. That's the sort of overly natural development the story had.
The only unnatural thing about it, then, was the fact that it wasn't the only natural development to occur.
Act One has ended. There's a ten minute break.
"Alright～! Things are going smoothly. We've completely hooked the audience!"
"Thanks for your hard work. Here, have a drink to stay hydrated."
"How are you holding up, Princess?"
"No problems. I told you right from the beginning."
"…Is that so? Alright, then."
"…Haah. How did I do? Do you think I need to act a little less high-spirited?"
"No, this feels just right for the first half. Your character's change between the first half and the climax sticks out more that way."
"What do you think, Senouchi-san? Were there any problems?"
"Kya!?"
"P-Princess…?"
"…Did I do something wrong? I can still correct whatever I need to right now, so please tell me."
"…Yoshida."
"Y-Yes…"
"H-Hey, you two… We should have the review meeting after the…"
"…That was perfect."
"…C-Come again?"
"This was pretty good for the opening act. You're not too fast nor too slow. It was easy for me to act with. Please continue like this."
"O-Okay…"
"No way… Was that a compliment?"
"And from Senouchi no less… that's quite amazing."
"Hey… then why are you in such a foul mood?"
"It's nothing… It's just something personal."
"Don't scare me like that… I almost froze on the spot."
"Anyway, I'm satisfied with our performance so far. …That being said, don't talk to me right now."
"P-Princess? What is that supposed to mean?"
"So the two of you have come together like some couple, eh…? So that's how it's going to be… You're trying to mess around with me…!"
"Senouchi-san…?"
"Fine, I see how it is… I'll let you see how great I really am, so you'd better enjoy it to the very end…!"
"Are you cold?"
"No, not at all. I'm actually feeling quite warm."
"…I suppose so."

The chairs have been taken out so that the hall could accommodate more viewers, but the number of spectators is completely beyond the venue's capacity anyway. The hall is just about packed to the brim.
Setsuna and I are among the crowd, and we're leaning against the wall at the back of the hall. We can feel the heat of the passionate performance even though the heating should be off.
The fact that a mere university drama club is able to incite such excitement among the crowd really speaks volumes about the troupe's talent.
…Or rather, it really speaks volumes about a certain someone's talent.
It's only natural… The opening act was little more than a generic romantic comedy, but it's really grabbed the crowd's attention and gotten a lot of laughs out of them.
"…Do you want to keep watching this?"
"…Yeah."
"Is that so…"
If we weren't already aware of how things will unfold from here… and if things unfolding in such a way didn't only serve to hurt us…
Perhaps we would've genuinely enjoyed this just a little more.
Act Two, Scene One.
The story progresses with the complex intersection of the relationship between Yukine and Kazuki, as well the relationship Kazuki shares with Haruna.
Yukine pouted like a child upon discovering that Kazuki and Haruna have been spending quite a lot of time alone together.
Kazuki was confused about the matter, given that it was the first time that he had seen a girl feeling jealous.
And the way he could only act flustered caused Yukine to feel even more irritated.

Haruna intervened and mediated things between the two, having felt exasperated by the ridiculous conflict between them, though she somehow also harbors feelings of uneasiness about the matter herself.
…At least, that's all I can say about this scene.
For some reason, I'm feeling incredibly embarrassed about how innocent the two actors are on stage.
And while I'm tilting my head downward, I cast a momentary, sideways glance…
And I notice that the person right next to me also has a bright red face, and her head is lowered at the same angle as mine.
Act Two, Scene Two.
"S-Stop… Don't look at it～!"
"I want to see it～!"
"I said no! I'm not finished with that yet… No, I didn't plan on showing this to anyone in the first place!"
"Let's see～ Todokanai Koi? W-Wow… Hey, are these lyrics by any chance!?"
"…If you don't know anything, then don't look at other people's notes, okay?"
"'Even if these feelings can never be conveyed, there will be a day where it can be reflected upon your heart'… Amazing… this is amazing, Kazuki-kun… You have an unexpected talent～"
"It's embarrassing, so please don't read it out loud…"
"This is… the song we'll perform for the competition, right? Which means I'll be the one singing it… Amazing!"
"Eh, ah, no… that's impossible. Everyone quit before the sheet music was written."
"Sheet music…?"
"The composition is missing… I've never done it before."
"Hmm…"
"I did hope that I would be able to fully complete it someday. Though given the way things are now, I doubt that'll happen any time soon."
"Speaking of which…"
"Hm?"
"It's been a while now… It's quite heavy, Kazuki-kun."
"Whoa!? I'm sorry, I'm sorry!"
The title of this story finally appeared in the middle of Act Two.
Act Two, Scene Three.
"You… this is…"
"Don't leave your notebook on the desk. I was so embarrassed reading it that I was thinking about tearing it up and throwing it away."
"I told you not to read my notebook without…"
"You never thought about the composition for a second, now, did you? It's so obvious that you're an amateur."
"Ugh…"

"…! Uu… hic… uug…"

"Why are you crying?"

"You're making me out to be quite terrible…"

Even though we're currently bickering with one another, I'm still grateful to God for allowing me to bear witness to this precious moment.
Because I've finally gotten to see it.

…Outside of the instances where she was acting, of course.
"I didn't think you'd run out while still wearing your costume… You'll freeze to death at this rate."
The moment I remove my coat, I am immediately blasted by the freezing wind and snow.

"…What's with that patronizing attitude of yours? I don't want it!"
"…Just shut up and put it on."
She really is an expert at reading others' hearts. She even saw through me as I tried to rub my moment of superiority in her face.
"Don't touch, don't touch me…! Stop patting my head and stop treating me like I'm some cat…!"
"Well, you're the one who started acting like a cat in the first place…"
As I slowly caress Chiaki's chilled cheeks and move down to the nape of her neck with my palms, I take in the sensation of her skin that I haven't gotten to feel in a long while.
…Yes, this is the sensation.

"…Wanna go back?"
"Where?"
"To my place, of course."
"I'll make sure to wake you up for tomorrow's public performance as well. You know how punctual I am, right?"
After savoring the feel of her neck and cheeks, I run my hand through her hair and dishevel it.
"Can you stand up? I'll call a taxi…"
"But you abandoned me."
"I'm getting really tired of that line."
"But you abandoned me and went back to Ogiso Setsuna."
"And that line really hurts, so stop it."
"Well, at least you're just feeling hurt. I'll have you know that I'm feeling nauseous, helpless and cold at the same time…"
"That's why we should hurry home, take a warm bath, and go to bed."
"But you abandoned me."
"Don't turn into a broken record, now."
"What are you trying to do…?"
"Huh?"
"Why are you showing up in front of me now? You were making fun of me with her during the performance."
"Because I abandoned someone."
"That's not an answer."
"It is…"
"How so…?"
"Because it's the opposite."
"Opposite…?"
"Because, believe it or not… I abandoned Setsuna to come back and get you."
"…Huh?"
"Fuuh, that was delicious."
"You really managed to finish the whole thing…"
"Is it really that surprising? A girl can eat this much too, you know."
"Well, if it weren't this cold out, that is…"
An empty parfait glass is in front of me.
While I'd completely lost interest in my coffee the moment it turned tepid, Setsuna thoroughly enjoyed her order of ice cream.
"I've been ordering this a lot whenever I come here with a friend of mine recently. It might have turned into a bit of a bad habit."
"Hmm…"
I can't properly discern anything from the expression Setsuna made when she muttered that.
"I wonder if it'll start snowing…"
"Cloudy with a chance of snowfall in the evening. That's what the weather forecast said, anyway."
"So it won't get much warmer, huh."
"It's usually like this throughout all of February, right?"
"Does that mean it'll get warmer tomorrow all of a sudden?"
"If the cold air followed a strict schedule, I suppose."
"Much like you do, Haruki-kun?"
"If it were me, the cold would've already been gone since yesterday. …It'd already be warmer by today."
"Hehe, that does sound like you."
"It's quite silly, though."
"Yeah… it sure is silly."
As silly as this might be, we're not bored by it.
We're not feeling bored even though we're only talking about the weather. If anything, we're happy to be able to have such a boring conversation.
It's already been three hours since I met up with Setsuna this afternoon. Time has passed miraculously smoothly between us.
Although my body feels cold, I'm slowly regaining the warmth in my heart.
If I can act like nothing happened, and just go back to our usual days…
"Do you have anything planned after this?"
"…No, nothing."
I hide both of my hands under the table.
What am I doing? Why am I looking at my watch while I'm spending time with Setsuna?
I'm not supposed to have any plans for later. There's no reason for me to be worrying about the time today.
…Isn't that right?
"Thank you for asking me out today. It was nice to see you after so long, Haruki-kun."
"Well, I… really wanted to see you too."
"We really do think alike, don't we?"
"Yeah…"
However, Setsuna continues talking to me in her usual manner, not noticing my frivolous movements.
She hasn't spoken a word about what happened that night. I'm not sure if she's forgotten or if she's just being considerate of me…
If I were to take it a step further and invite her to dinner after this, would Setsuna be bothered by my invitation?
Or would she instead smile as easily as she is now, then ask me, "Why do you need to ask me about something like that at this point?" while nodding, as if it were the most natural thing in the world?
"Setsuna."
"What is it?"
No… that's not it.
I need to make up my mind. Both of us are fully aware of that.
That's why we're able to spend time together like this right now, peacefully and uneventfully.
I'm sure that if I were to run away without another word, Setsuna would be ready to accept that it would mean absolutely nothing at all.
…And she must believe that I'm not the kind of person who'd allow himself to make use of such a convenient lapse in memory to run away.
That's why… I just can't betray the faith that Setsuna has in me.
"Let's… make this the last time the two of us meet alone."
Which is why I have no choice… but to betray Setsuna.
As if the cold from outside had seeped into the cafe, time froze still between us.
"It's not that I think that she can't go on without me… and it's not that I think you'll be just fine without me either, Setsuna."
However, I force my numb lips open to speak.
"I imagine she will keep toying with me. She might even betray me again. And I'm probably in for more painful experiences with her…"
My words come out like icy blades, leaving wounds all over my mouth…
"But… I still think it's more pleasant than betraying you, Setsuna."
"And it's not as painful as… being with you, Setsuna…"
And they proceed to tear Setsuna into shreds.
"After all, all I'd ever have to do is get back on my own two feet again."
Our surroundings fall into absolute silence the moment I stop talking.
Setsuna's staring at me without a word, and I can't tell what thoughts lie behind her expression at all.
…And I'm sure she's desperately trying to keep it that way.
Nevertheless, she seems to have no intention of interrupting me or objecting to what I just said.
"I don't want to hurt you anymore, Setsuna. Because I know I'll only keep inflicting wounds upon myself that will never heal if this goes on."
And so I callously continue to hurt Setsuna and recite words meant to tear the two of us apart.
"I know how incredibly selfish this is. But I won't change what I've decided on."
Because this is… the last time I'll have to do it.
"And the reason why I was able to make such a foolish decision… of course, wasn't just you, Setsuna…"
"…Chiaki-san."
"That's right. It's because I love her."
It's precisely because this will be the last time I have to do it that I'm inflicting Setsuna with the gravest wound possible.
"She tricked me and hurt me as well. She's a horrible woman… But none of the moments I spent with her were this painful. I wanted them to last forever."
And in doing so, my entire body is stained in red.
Though I no longer know if the blood that's been spilled is Setsuna's or mine.
"Mmm…"
At last, Setsuna opens her mouth.
Though the words that followed were not intended to curse me or express regret at what I just said.
"Look, I finished it."
On the tip of her tongue, there's a knot she made from the stem of the cherry that came with her parfait.
It's a very tight knot.
"Hey, Haruki-kun."
And I'm sure that I'll never be able to understand the meaning behind that gesture, no matter how much time passes.
"Do you want to go watch Chiaki-san's play? We can still make it in time before the show starts, right?"
"So you knew…"
"Let's go and confirm them, then… Her true feelings."
Chiaki is hugging her own shoulders.
She's tightly clinging onto the coat that I've given her.
"Stand up."
"Why?"
"I can't hug you while you're on the ground."
"…Uu, aha, ahaha…"
"What's so funny?"
"Ahaha… you got tricked. Haruki, you got tricked again～"
Just like that, Chiaki starts ridiculing me, as she usually does.
But her hands, stuck to the ground, are still shaking.
She desperately straightens her elbows while getting up on one knee and gritting her teeth, causing her to spill even more tears.
As her hands finally break away from the ground, she places them on her knees to support herself and force her exhausted body to stand up…
Only to fall back to her knees again after running out of strength.
"Chiaki…"
"Don't touch me!"
Unable to keep watching her like this, I attempt to lift her up with my arms, but Chiaki rejects me with a loud voice that strains her body to its limits.
"…! Haah, haah, haah…"
"But aren't you in pain?"
"What do you think…? This is the first time in my life I've completely lost control of my body like this."
"Then let me…"
"Didn't you say that… I have to stand up on my own, Haruki? That if I manage to stand up… you'll forgive everything."
"I never said that."
"Even so, I'll bear it and stand up on my own… So, please… please…"
"There's no way I'd forgive you that easily."
"Please… hold me tight."
Chiaki stood up using her own strength.
But the next moment, she ran out of strength and collapsed into my arms.
"Uu… hic… uu, uuu…!"
"I'm the one who should be crying here…"
Chiaki finally stood up because she believed that she would be rewarded by me, and so I respond by embracing her with all of my strength.
"Nya, nyaaaa…"
"Oh, there, there…"
"Mew… meew… uwaaaa… uwaaaaa!"

I'm an idiot. I'm an even bigger idiot than she is.

…Well, more precisely, I should be saying that she's shown me a "Yukine" that I can believe in.
"Ah… Haruki."
"Hmm…?"

"Don't even think about touching me there at a time like this."

"Wait, so were you… really going at it during that kiss scene earlier…?"
"I'm going to drive you wild with jealousy, Haruki. I won't tell you anything until you ki… Mmph!"

"Nn, nnn… hwa, aah… Nn… nnn… nnnn…!"
Chiaki's lips feel so hot they could burn me.
"It's snowing."

"Setsuna…"
